title: Mall World Poem
content: In my dreams, I wonder through a towering mall, Where I feel small, beneath its grand sprawl. Through sliding doors, I softly glide, Seeking solace, nowhere to hide. Amongst towering shelves of books, I find refuge in hidden nooks. Upstairs, a grand hall awaits, With treats from lands and distant states. Yet through a door, to my dissmany, A bathroom, in disarray. Dirty floors, and waterdeep, Through the mess, I try to creep. Lost in labyrinth halls, I roam, No exit found, for from home. Trapped within capitalismis grasp, In this dream, my fate I clasp.
